passages.text: Then Job replied: “If only my grief could be weighed and placed with my calamity on the scales.
passages.sermon:
Job was a man who suffered greatly.
Job replied to his friends.
Job said, "I wish someone could weigh my grief."
I want my sorrow to be measured.
I want my calamity to be placed on the scales with my grief.
I want both my grief and my calamity to be weighed together.
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ ל֗וּ שָׁק֣וֹל יִשָּׁקֵ֣ל כַּעְשִׂ֑י וְהַיָּתִי בְּֽמֹאזְנַ֥יִם יִשְׂאוּ־ יָֽחַד׃

passages.text: For then it would outweigh the sand of the seas— no wonder my words have been rash.
passages.sermon:
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
\r\nHe speaks about his pain.
\r\nHe says his grief is very heavy.
\r\nHis grief is heavier than the sand by the sea.
\r\nHis words have been rash.
\r\nHis pain explains why he spoke this way.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ עַתָּ֗ה מֵח֣וֹל יַמִּ֣ים יִכְבָּ֑ד עַל־ כֵּ֝֗ן דְּבָרַ֥י לָֽעוּ׃

passages.text: For the arrows of the Almighty have pierced me; my spirit drinks in their poison; the terrors of God are arrayed against me.
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking.
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
The Almighty is God.
God has sent arrows against Job.
These arrows have pierced Job.
The poison from these arrows fills Job’s spirit.
God’s terrors stand in order against Job.
passages.original: כִּ֤י חִצֵּ֪י שַׁדַּ֡י עִמָּדִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֲ֭מָתָם שֹׁתָ֣ה רוּחִ֑י בִּעוּתֵ֖י אֱל֣וֹהַּ יַֽעַרְכֽוּנִי׃

passages.text: Does a wild donkey bray over fresh grass, or an ox low over its fodder?
passages.sermon: A wild donkey does not bray when it has fresh grass.\r\nAn ox does not low when it has its fodder.
passages.original: הֲיִֽנְהַק־ פֶּ֥רֶא עֲלֵי־ דֶ֑שֶׁא אִ֥ם יִגְעֶה־ שּׁ֝֗וֹר עַל־ בְּלִילֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Is tasteless food eaten without salt, or is there flavor in the white of an egg ?
passages.sermon:
Tasteless food has no salt.
People do not eat tasteless food without salt.
The white of an egg has no flavor.
There is no taste in the white of an egg.
passages.original: הֲיֵאָכֵ֣ל תָּ֭פֵל מִבְּלִי־ מֶ֑לַח אִם־ יֶשׁ־ טַ֝֗עַם בְּרִ֣יר חַלָּמֽוּת׃

passages.text: My soul refuses to touch them; they are loathsome food to me.
passages.sermon:
Job is the speaker.
Job suffers greatly.
Job feels deep anguish.
Job says, "My soul refuses to touch these things."
Job calls them loathsome food to him.
passages.original: מֵאֲנָ֣ה לִנְגּ֣וֹעַ נַפְשִׁ֑י הֵ֝֗מָּה כִּדְוֵ֥י לַחְמִֽי׃

passages.text: If only my request were granted and God would fulfill my hope: that God would be willing to crush me, to unleash His hand and cut me off!
passages.sermon:
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
\r\nHe speaks to God.
\r\nJob wishes that God would answer his request.
\r\nHe hopes God will give him what he asks.
\r\nJob wants God to be willing to crush him.
\r\nHe asks God to use His power against him.
\r\nJob wants God to cut off his life.
passages.original: מִֽי־ יִ֭תֵּן תָּב֣וֹא שֶֽׁאֱלָתִ֑י וְ֝תִקְוָתִ֗י יִתֵּ֥ן אֱלֽוֹהַּ׃ וְיֹאֵ֣ל אֱ֭לוֹהַּ וִֽידַכְּאֵ֑נִי יַתֵּ֥ר יָ֝ד֗וֹ וִֽיבַצְּעֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: It still brings me comfort, and joy through unrelenting pain, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
passages.sermon:
Job is suffering greatly.
He feels deep pain that does not stop.
He finds comfort in one thing.
He has not denied the words of the Holy One.
He feels joy because he stayed faithful.
He did not hide or reject God’s words.
passages.original: וּ֥תְהִי ע֨וֹד׀ נֶ֘חָ֤מָתִ֗י וַאֲסַלְּדָ֣ה בְ֭חִילָה לֹ֣א יַחְמ֑וֹל כִּי־ לֹ֥א כִ֝חַ֗דְתִּי אִמְרֵ֥י קָדֽוֹשׁ׃

passages.text: What strength do I have, that I should still hope? What is my future, that I should be patient?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in deep suffering.
Job feels weak and hopeless.
Job asks, “What strength do I have?”
Job wonders, “Why should I keep hoping?”
Job asks, “What future is left for me?”
Job questions, “Why should I wait any longer?”
passages.original: מַה־ כֹּחִ֥י כִֽי־ אֲיַחֵ֑ל וּמַה־ קִּ֝צִּ֗י כִּֽי־ אַאֲרִ֥יךְ נַפְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: Is my strength like that of stone, or my flesh made of bronze?
passages.sermon:
Job is a man who suffers greatly.
He speaks about his weakness.
He asks a question.
He says, "Is my strength like the strength of stones?"
He also asks, "Is my flesh made of bronze?"
He means that he is not unbreakable or unfeeling.
He is not as strong as stone or bronze.
He is only human.
passages.original: אִם־ כֹּ֣חַ אֲבָנִ֣ים כֹּחִ֑י אִֽם־ בְּשָׂרִ֥י נָחֽוּשׁ׃

passages.text: Is there any help within me now that success is driven from me?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks in his suffering.
He feels weak and abandoned.
He asks, “Is there any help left in me?”
He says, “My strength is gone.”
He says, “Success has left me.”
He wonders if he has any power or wisdom left.
passages.original: הַאִ֬ם אֵ֣ין עֶזְרָתִ֣י בִ֑י וְ֝תֻשִׁיָּ֗ה נִדְּחָ֥ה מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

passages.text: A despairing man should have the kindness of his friend, even if he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
passages.sermon: A man who is in despair needs kindness from his friend.\r\nHe needs this kindness even if he has turned away from the fear of the Almighty.
passages.original: לַמָּ֣ס מֵרֵעֵ֣הוּ חָ֑סֶד וְיִרְאַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י יַעֲזֽוֹב׃

passages.text: But my brothers are as faithless as wadis, as seasonal streams that overflow, darkened because of the ice and the inflow of melting snow, but ceasing in the dry season and vanishing from their channels in the heat.
passages.sermon:
My brothers have betrayed me.
They act like wadis.
Wadis are dry riverbeds.
Wadis fill with water only in certain seasons.
My brothers are like streams that overflow for a time.
These streams become dark from ice.
Melting snow covers them.
When the dry season comes, these streams disappear.
In the heat, they vanish from their places.
My brothers are not faithful.
They are not dependable.
They are present only for a short time, like seasonal streams.
passages.original: אַ֭חַי בָּגְד֣וּ כְמוֹ־ נָ֑חַל כַּאֲפִ֖יק נְחָלִ֣ים יַעֲבֹֽרוּ׃ הַקֹּדְרִ֥ים מִנִּי־ קָ֑רַח עָ֝לֵ֗ימוֹ יִתְעַלֶּם־ שָֽׁלֶג׃ בְּ֭עֵת יְזֹרְב֣וּ נִצְמָ֑תוּ בְּ֝חֻמּ֗וֹ נִדְעֲכ֥וּ מִמְּקוֹמָֽם׃

passages.text: Caravans turn aside from their routes; they go into the wasteland and perish.
passages.sermon:
Caravans travel together.
Caravans follow a set route.
Sometimes, caravans leave their route.
They turn aside from their path.
They enter the wasteland.
They go into empty, dangerous places.
They lose their way.
They perish there.
passages.original: יִ֭לָּ֣פְתוּ אָרְח֣וֹת דַּרְכָּ֑ם יַעֲל֖וּ בַתֹּ֣הוּ וְיֹאבֵֽדוּ׃

passages.text: The caravans of Tema look for water; the travelers of Sheba hope to find it.
passages.sermon:
The caravans of Tema travel through the land.
These caravans search for water.
The travelers from Sheba journey on their way.
These travelers hope to find water.
passages.original: הִ֭בִּיטוּ אָרְח֣וֹת תֵּמָ֑א הֲלִיכֹ֥ת שְׁ֝בָ֗א קִוּוּ־ לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: They are confounded because they had hoped; their arrival brings disappointment.
passages.sermon:
The travelers hoped for something good.
They trusted they would find what they needed.
They arrived at their destination.
They felt ashamed.
They were disappointed.
passages.original: בֹּ֥שׁוּ כִּֽי־ בָטָ֑ח בָּ֥אוּ עָ֝דֶ֗יהָ וַיֶּחְפָּֽרוּ׃

passages.text: For now you are of no help; you see terror, and you are afraid.
passages.sermon:
You are my friends.
You are not helping me now.
You see something frightening.
You become afraid.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ עַ֭תָּה הֱיִ֣יתֶם לֹא תִּֽרְא֥וּ חֲ֝תַ֗ת וַתִּירָֽאוּ׃

passages.text: Have I ever said, ‘Give me something; offer me a bribe from your wealth; deliver me from the hand of the enemy; redeem me from the grasp of the ruthless’?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
Job is suffering.
Job asks a question.
He says, “Did I ever ask you for anything?”
He says, “Did I say, ‘Give me something?’”
He says, “Did I ask you to offer me a gift from your wealth?”
He says, “Did I ask you to rescue me from an enemy?”
He says, “Did I ask you to save me from the hand of the ruthless?”
passages.original: הֲ‍ֽכִי־ אָ֭מַרְתִּי הָ֣בוּ לִ֑י וּ֝מִכֹּחֲכֶ֗ם שִׁחֲד֥וּ בַעֲדִֽי׃ וּמַלְּט֥וּנִי מִיַּד־ צָ֑ר וּמִיַּ֖ד עָרִיצִ֣ים תִּפְדּֽוּנִי׃

passages.text: Teach me, and I will be silent. Help me understand how I have erred.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
Job asks for instruction.
He says, "Teach me."
He promises, "I will be silent."
He asks for understanding.
He says, "Help me know how I have done wrong."
passages.original: ה֭וֹרוּנִי וַאֲנִ֣י אַחֲרִ֑ישׁ וּמַה־ שָּׁ֝גִ֗יתִי הָבִ֥ינוּ לִֽי׃

passages.text: How painful are honest words! But what does your argument prove?
passages.sermon: Honest words can cause pain.\r\nYour argument does not prove anything.\r\n
passages.original: מַה־ נִּמְרְצ֥וּ אִמְרֵי־ יֹ֑שֶׁר וּמַה־ יּוֹכִ֖יחַ הוֹכֵ֣חַ מִכֶּֽם׃

passages.text: Do you intend to correct my words, and treat as wind my cry of despair?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
Job suffers greatly.
Job feels deep despair.
Job asks his friends a question.
He says, “Do you want to correct my words?”
He says, “Do you think my words are only words?”
He says, “Do you treat my cry of despair as nothing?”
He says, “Do you ignore my pain?”
passages.original: הַלְהוֹכַ֣ח מִלִּ֣ים תַּחְשֹׁ֑בוּ וּ֝לְר֗וּחַ אִמְרֵ֥י נֹאָֽשׁ׃

passages.text: You would even cast lots for an orphan and barter away your friend.
passages.sermon:
You act without mercy.
You would gamble for an orphan.
You would trade away your friend.
You treat the vulnerable with injustice.
You betray those close to you.
passages.original: אַף־ עַל־ יָת֥וֹם תַּפִּ֑ילוּ וְ֝תִכְר֗וּ עַל־ רֵֽיעֲכֶֽם׃

passages.text: But now, please look at me. Would I lie to your face?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
Job feels misunderstood.
Job asks his friends to look at him.
Job says, "Please turn to me."
Job asks, "Would I lie to your face?"
passages.original: וְ֭עַתָּה הוֹאִ֣ילוּ פְנוּ־ בִ֑י וְעַל־ פְּ֝נֵיכֶ֗ם אִם־ אֲכַזֵּֽב׃

passages.text: Reconsider; do not be unjust. Reconsider, for my righteousness is at stake.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
He asks them to reconsider their actions.
He tells them not to be unjust.
He urges them to think again.
He says his righteousness is at stake.
passages.original: שֻֽׁבוּ־ נָ֭א אַל־ תְּהִ֣י עַוְלָ֑ה וְשֻׁבִי ע֝וֹד צִדְקִי־ בָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Is there iniquity on my tongue? Can my mouth not discern malice?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
Job asks a question about himself.
Job says, "Is there iniquity on my tongue?"
Job asks, "Does my mouth fail to recognize evil?"
passages.original: הֲיֵשׁ־ בִּלְשׁוֹנִ֥י עַוְלָ֑ה אִם־ חִ֝כִּ֗י לֹא־ יָבִ֥ין הַוּֽוֹת׃
